# LateApexEarlySpeed JSON Schema and JSON Assertion Packages

This repository contains three primary public packages for JSON Schema validation and JSON assertions in .NET:

- LateApexEarlySpeed.Json.Schema
- LateApexEarlySpeed.Xunit.Assertion.Json
- LateApexEarlySpeed.Xunit.V3.Assertion.Json

Other projects in this repository are support, benchmark, or unrelated package projects and are not part of this AI usage map.

## Package Map

### LateApexEarlySpeed.Json.Schema

Install:

```powershell
Install-Package LateApexEarlySpeed.Json.Schema
```

Primary namespaces:

```csharp
using LateApexEarlySpeed.Json.Schema;
using LateApexEarlySpeed.Json.Schema.Common;
using LateApexEarlySpeed.Json.Schema.FluentGenerator;
using LateApexEarlySpeed.Json.Schema.Generator;
using LateApexEarlySpeed.Json.Schema.Keywords;
```

Primary APIs:

- JsonValidator: validate JSON instances against a JSON Schema.
- JsonValidatorOptions: configure schema parsing, default dialect, annotations, custom keywords, and custom formats.
- JsonSchemaOptions: configure per-validation behavior such as output format, format validation, regex timeout, and error-message generation.
- ValidationResult: inspect IsValid, ValidationErrors, and Annotations.
- JsonSchemaBuilder: build a JsonValidator with fluent C# validation rules.
- JsonSchemaGenerator: generate a JsonValidator from a .NET type.
- FormatRegistry and FormatValidator: add custom format validation.

Common rules:

- Create one JsonValidator per schema and reuse it for repeated validation.
- Use JsonValidatorOptions.DefaultDialect when schema text has no $schema.
- Use JsonSchemaOptions.OutputFormat = OutputFormat.List when the caller needs all validation errors or annotation collection.
- Set JsonValidatorOptions.CollectAnnotations = true and validate with OutputFormat.List to collect annotations.
- Register external schemas with AddExternalDocument before validating schemas that use external $ref values.
- Use JsonSchemaBuilder when the user wants to express validation rules in C# instead of raw JSON Schema text.
- Use JsonSchemaGenerator.GenerateJsonValidator<T>() when the user wants to create a validator from .NET type shape.
- Use options.FormatRegistry.AddFormat(...) to register custom formats for a specific validator instance.

Important limitations:

- unevaluatedProperties is not supported.
- unevaluatedItems is not supported.
- Automatic content-encoded string decoding and validation is not currently supported.
- GetStandardJsonSchemaText() can throw NotSupportedException when the validator contains extended keywords from some fluent/custom/type-based construction paths.

### LateApexEarlySpeed.Xunit.Assertion.Json

Install for xUnit v2 tests:

```powershell
Install-Package LateApexEarlySpeed.Xunit.Assertion.Json
```

Primary namespace:

```csharp
using LateApexEarlySpeed.Xunit.Assertion.Json;
```

Primary APIs:

- JsonAssertion.Meet(...): assert JSON shape and values with the same fluent rule style as the validator builder.
- JsonAssertion.Equivalent(...): assert JSON equivalence.
- JsonAssertionOptions: configure JSON array and string comparison behavior.
- JsonAssertException: assertion failure with JSON Pointer locations.

Use this package in projects that use xUnit v2.

### LateApexEarlySpeed.Xunit.V3.Assertion.Json

Install for xUnit v3 tests:

```powershell
Install-Package LateApexEarlySpeed.Xunit.V3.Assertion.Json
```

Primary namespace:

```csharp
using LateApexEarlySpeed.Xunit.V3.Assertion.Json;
```

Primary APIs:

- JsonAssertion.Meet(...): assert JSON shape and values with the same fluent rule style as the validator builder.
- JsonAssertion.Equivalent(...): assert JSON equivalence.
- JsonAssertionOptions: configure JSON array and string comparison behavior.
- JsonAssertException: assertion failure with JSON Pointer locations.

Use this package in projects that use xUnit v3.

## Choose The API

- User has JSON Schema text and JSON instance text: use new JsonValidator(schema).Validate(instance).
- User validates many instances with the same schema: create one JsonValidator and reuse it.
- User wants all errors: pass new JsonSchemaOptions { OutputFormat = OutputFormat.List } to Validate.
- User has no $schema and needs a specific dialect: pass new JsonValidatorOptions { DefaultDialect = DialectKind.Draft7 } or another DialectKind.
- User wants validation rules in C#: use JsonSchemaBuilder and BuildValidator().
- User wants a validator from a C# type: use JsonSchemaGenerator.GenerateJsonValidator<T>().
- User writes xUnit v2 tests: install LateApexEarlySpeed.Xunit.Assertion.Json and use LateApexEarlySpeed.Xunit.Assertion.Json.
- User writes xUnit v3 tests: install LateApexEarlySpeed.Xunit.V3.Assertion.Json and use LateApexEarlySpeed.Xunit.V3.Assertion.Json.
